brief: A PLA dumbbell: a bar 50 mm long and 10 mm square, with a 16 mm ball centred on each end of it. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: A small decorative or display object shaped like a dumbbell: a square bar with a ball centered at each end, intended to carry no functional load.
intent.part_kind: decorative/novelty model (dumbbell-shaped bar with ball ends)
stated: A 16 mm ball is centred on each end of the bar
It carries no load, so there is no load case
implied: Since it's PLA and explicitly stated to carry no load, it is likely a display/decorative piece or printed demo model rather than a functional mechanical component
'Centred on each end' implies the ball's center axis aligns with the bar's central axis, requiring the balls to be symmetric about the bar's cross-section centroid
Likely intended for 3D printing given PLA material callout
unstated: Whether the balls and bar are a single continuous printed part or separate assembled components
The fillet/blend radius or transition geometry where the square bar meets the spherical ball ends
Tolerances on the 50 mm length, 10 mm square section, and 16 mm ball diameter
Orientation for printing (if intended for 3D printing) and any print-specific requirements like layer adhesion direction
Any handling, aesthetic, or packaging requirements
Whether 'no load' also excludes handling loads, drop impacts, or shipping stresses (even non-functional parts experience incidental handling forces)
Color or finish of the PLA
out_of_scope: Any load-bearing analysis, since the brief explicitly states there is no load case
Material strength properties beyond identifying PLA as the stated material

requirements.statement: The connecting bar shall be 50 mm long.
requirements.rationale: Brief states the bar is 50 mm long.

requirements.statement: The bar shall have a square cross-section 10 mm on a side.
requirements.rationale: Brief states the bar is 10 mm square in cross-section.

requirements.statement: Each ball end shall be 16 mm in diameter.
requirements.rationale: Brief states a 16 mm ball at each end of the bar.

requirements.statement: There shall be exactly two ball ends, one centred on each end of the bar.
requirements.rationale: Brief describes a ball centred on each of the bar's two ends.

assumptions.statement: The part is modelled in PLA with no special grade or additive called out; this is recorded in the component's material field, not as a dimensional requirement.
assumptions.rationale: Brief names PLA explicitly as the material.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Negligible -- PLA is explicitly stated, this assumption only governs how it is recorded.

assumptions.statement: The bar-to-ball transition at each end is a simple tangent/smooth blend typical of a printed dumbbell shape, with no separate fillet dimension called out.
assumptions.rationale: Brief gives no fillet or blend radius between the square bar and the spherical ends.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A sharp, undefined junction could create a stress riser or print artefact, though this is cosmetic given the no-load case.

assumptions.statement: The dumbbell is produced as a single, continuous printed part (bar and both balls as one solid), not an assembly of separate components.
assumptions.rationale: Brief describes one dumbbell shape with no mention of assembly or fasteners.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If separate parts were intended, interface and attachment features would be needed that are absent from this design.

assumptions.statement: Standard FDM/PLA printing tolerance (approx. +/-0.2 mm) applies to all dimensions; no tight tolerance is called out.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Tighter tolerance needs would require secondary machining or a different process, not indicated by the brief.

assumptions.statement: One unit of the dumbbell is to be produced/modelled.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Irrelevant to the geometric design itself; only affects production planning.

document.name: Dumbbell display bar
document.description: Decorative dumbbell: a square-section bar with a sphere centred on each end, printed as one continuous PLA body. Carries no load; all dimensions are driven by named parameters so bar length, section size and ball diameter can be changed together without breaking alignment.

parameters.description: Length of the connecting bar, along X
Side length of the bar's square cross-section (Y and Z)
Cosmetic fillet radius where the bar meets each ball; not called out in the brief, chosen purely for a smooth printable junction since the part is non-load-bearing.

features.description: Square-section connecting bar, centred on the origin along X
Ball centred on the left (negative X) end of the bar
Ball centred on the right (positive X) end of the bar
Bar and both ball ends joined into the single printed body

answer.rationale: The dumbbell is built from three primitives -- one centred box for the bar (its thinnest/square section in Y and Z) and two spheres placed symmetrically at +-bar_length/2 so the ball centres stay on the bar's axis and end faces regardless of parameter changes -- joined by a single blended union that is the part's one terminal solid. bar_length, bar_cross_section_side and ball_diameter are declared exactly as required and drive every position by expression; the only invented value is a small cosmetic transition_blend_radius for a printable junction, called out as a bounded, optimizable parameter rather than baked into geometry, consistent with the brief's explicit no-load statement. Each sphere carries the "ball_end" tag so the feature-count requirement sees exactly two, and the union itself is untagged.
